references.text: Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim is mentioned as one of the cities of refuge, also noted in Joshua 21:21.
Jacob came to Shechem in the land of Canaan, which shows Shechem's historical significance as an important city.
Jacob gave Joseph Shechem as a special inheritance portion, explaining why Shechem became a Levitical city within the territory of the tribe of Ephraim.
The Lord commanded that cities of refuge be designated for those who kill unintentionally, and Shechem served this purpose according to Joshua 21:21.
Gezer is mentioned as a city within the territory of Ephraim, even though the Canaanites were not driven out from there.
Pharaoh captured Gezer and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife, showing Gezer's continued importance.
A parallel passage confirms that Shechem with its pasture lands in the hill country of Ephraim was given to the sons of Kohath.
